messages.text:
Ok, now we need to move on to Tracker reconstruction, take the current baseline, Fatras, smeared digitization and create a full reconstruction pipeline for the Tracker, first keeping the single muon target (1,5,10,100 GeV pT).

For ACTS try to use and tune the GBTS seeder to maximise the efficiency, while minimizing the fake rate.

I’ll use the balanced baseline with a constant 3 T field, Fatras and smeared digitization, adding 5 GeV to the single-muon samples. I’ll check ACTS GBTS support, build the reconstruction chain, and tune it on separate training and validation samples while tracking efficiency, fake rate and duplicate rate.

PR #104 is merged, so I’ll start from that balanced baseline. I’m using the project’s ACTS environment and validation workflow, with separate implementation and physics-review assignments. Truth will be used for GBTS connection training and performance scoring; the reconstruction chain will use hit-based seeds.

The Spack preflight reports changed setup/lock fingerprints and cannot verify full DD4hep/Geant4 source trees. I’ll check the installed runtime directly before using it and keep reconstruction builds in task-owned directories.

The installed ACTS runtime has GBTS, CKF and ambiguity resolution support. The standard GBTS example contains ITk-specific layer rules, so I’m adding a thin adapter around the ACTS core seeder for this Gen-3 geometry. The native chain will remain pixel space points → GBTS seeds → CKF over all tracker measurements → ambiguity resolution.

The review identified two checks for the new chain: matching must use the same generated-muon denominator before and after ambiguity resolution, and GBTS must explicitly receive the 3 T field. I’ll also separate secondary tracks from fakes and show efficiency across the full |η| ≤ 4 range, including 5 GeV.

The GBTS adapter now compiles against the installed ACTS runtime and produces seeds in synthetic helix checks at all four momenta and central/forward angles. Next I’ll test the full Fatras chain to see where tracks are lost: seeding, parameter estimation, CKF, or ambiguity resolution.

The freshly prepared material map and Gaussian response match the retained balanced-baseline payloads exactly. The native audit is also built; it will retain every event and source link so missed tracks and unclassified candidates stay in the performance denominators.

The first complete native run succeeded. In this ten-event smoke sample, the initial GBTS settings seed the forward tracks but miss the barrel tracks. I’ll investigate that before running the larger scan; the event records show the missed tracks have pixel hits available.

The barrel loss comes from GBTS’s optional innermost-layer z₀ histogram. Disabling it restores seeds for the four-layer barrel tracks in the smoke sample; a separate three-layer setting is needed where the fourth pixel layer is missed. I’ll retain the original control and test both settings in the bounded scan before choosing a configuration for validation.

The 13-profile scan is complete. The selected configuration uses a 0.4 GeV GBTS threshold, nominal tau cuts, three-layer recovery and the z₀ histogram disabled. On 500 tuning events per momentum, efficiency is 96.6%, 100%, 99.8% and 100%, with no observed fakes or duplicates.

I’ll freeze it for independent validation. I’ll also report wrong-charge fits separately: they appear at 100 GeV in the far-forward region even when the measurements are correctly associated.

The larger validation jobs stopped on floating-point exceptions with the optional native ROOT state writer enabled; the tuning runs did not encounter them. I’ll locate the exceptions and resolve the output issue while keeping the reconstruction settings and FPE checks unchanged.

The traces isolate the exceptions to ACTS’s optional `RootTrackStatesWriter`. I’ll retain state parameters in the native audit and keep the ROOT summaries and measurements. FPE checks will stay enabled. The final runs will use a fresh validation seed with the frozen reconstruction cuts unchanged.

The fresh validation runs completed with FPE checks enabled. Over 5,000 muons per momentum, the frozen configuration reaches 97.18%, 99.28%, 99.30% and 99.44% efficiency at 1, 5, 10 and 100 GeV. There are four unmatched candidates across the 20,000 selected-profile events and no duplicates.

I’ll finish the resolution and pull plots, then have the exact results and provenance independently checked.

The plots are ready. All four unmatched candidates use primary-muon hits but fail the fixed 50% completeness requirement; the report distinguishes those from mixed-origin combinations. It also retains the main fit limitations: broader q/p pull tails at 1 GeV and a 1.91% wrong-charge fraction at 100 GeV, concentrated forward.

Both independent reviews have reproduced the held-out results. The scientific reviewer reclassified all 40,000 selected/control event entries and matched every retained count and representative track. The software reviewer replayed all eight validation outputs exactly. I’m finishing the build guards and project records, then preparing the draft `Tracker:` PR.

The reconstruction and validation are complete. The GitHub integration could not create the draft PR because of its permissions, so I’m using the authenticated CLI to publish it and finish the discussion and accounting records.

Draft [PR #107](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/107) is open. Held-out efficiencies are 97.18%, 99.28%, 99.30% and 99.44% at 1, 5, 10 and 100 GeV. No duplicates survive ambiguity resolution; the report also retains four partial-track mismatches and the forward wrong-charge tail at 100 GeV.

The first CI failure is the expected missing interaction record for the newly assigned PR number. That record is now added. I’ve also verified the coordinator and specialist thread identities; exact token counters are unavailable, so the accounting records state that gap explicitly.

The interaction and accounting CI job now passes. The remaining CI jobs are running the project controls and replaying the retained plots. The pipeline, tuning scan, full residuals and pulls, and execution guide are all in PR #107.

CI has passed the project records, workflow checks and material-profile replays. It is still running geometry controls and tracking-performance replays. The main remaining physics limitation is forward momentum and charge reconstruction at 100 GeV, despite the high matching efficiency.

The tracking CI job has passed, including the GBTS evidence verifier and plot replay. The accounting job is also green. Only the broader geometry and project-control job remains before I close the session record.

The remaining job has passed the balanced-baseline and TDR fingerprint checks. The frozen GBTS settings are unchanged: a 0.4 GeV threshold, nominal tau cuts, three-layer recovery and the optional z₀ histogram disabled.

The reconstruction result is ready for expert review. The execution guide documents rerunning the native chain and replaying the retained data. The session records link the independent physics and software assessments; human review remains pending.
All geometry controls have passed. CI is finishing documentation-link and environment checks; I’ll then close the journal and push the final metadata update.

The final CI job is now in the repository-record tests. Native tracking, plot replays, geometry controls and accounting have passed. I refreshed the public PR discussion as part of closeout; there are no reviewer comments yet.
All CI jobs passed at `8d4d95c`. I’m closing the journal and synchronizing the final PR snapshot. The remaining push contains only project, discussion and accounting records.

Implemented in draft [PR #107](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/107).

The balanced baseline now runs **Fatras → smeared digitization → measured pixel space points → native GBTS → CKF over all tracker systems → ambiguity resolution**, using constant 3 T.

After tuning 13 configurations, the frozen configuration achieved these held-out results with **5,000 muons per momentum**, |η| ≤ 4:

| pT [GeV] | Efficiency | Unmatched accepted tracks |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 97.18% | 1 |
| 5 | 99.28% | 1 |
| 10 | 99.30% | 2 |
| 100 | 99.44% | 0 |

No duplicates survive ambiguity resolution. The four unmatched tracks are incomplete primary trajectories. Remaining limitations include **1.91% wrong charge at 100 GeV**, concentrated forward, and broader low-momentum pull tails.

[Full results, resolutions and pulls]([redacted]

Native validation, independent reviews and CI passed. The final metadata-only CI rerun is pending. Discussion/accounting records are updated; exact token counters were unavailable.
